guard: overlapping hook frames count ownership of the same surfaced ids so one delivery verdict cannot release another frame's protection
why: The old cell inferred a refcount property from later overflow eviction and JetStream redelivery timing. It failed nondeterministically on unrelated branches because the selected live-inbox batch could change during redelivery.

The replacement drives the MeshAgent hold/release state machine directly with a unique synthetic id. Existing boolean observability is sufficient: after two holds, the first release must leave the id protected and the second must release it.

W1 restores boolean-set behavior: the second frame no longer increments an existing hold. W2 makes the first verdict delete the hold regardless of the second frame. Both must red at the surviving-protection cell.

mutations.name: W1 a second overlapping frame does not increment the existing hold
mutations.expectRed: one frame's verdict does not unprotect the overlapping id
mutations.cell: one frame's verdict does not unprotect the overlapping id
mutations.note: Recreates the boolean hold that let one frame's verdict speak for another.

mutations.name: W2 the first frame verdict releases an id another frame still holds
mutations.expectRed: one frame's verdict does not unprotect the overlapping id
mutations.cell: one frame's verdict does not unprotect the overlapping id
mutations.note: Recreates the premature release the counted hold prevents.
